```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all("~/Documents/Research/Code/ECE")
library(tidyverse)
```

`scenario(scenario_num, ...)` builds the parameter list for one of five mean-shift patterns used throughout the simulation studies. Each scenario adds a different nonstationary mean $h(t)$ on top of correlated errors $\varepsilon_t$, so that $X_t = h(t) + \varepsilon_t$. The goal of ECE is to remain valid for testing $\text{Cor}(X)$ under all of these mean patterns without explicitly modeling $h(t)$.

For each scenario below we fix `n=1000`, `r=0`, `amp=1` and show two diagnostics: the generated data `X` (colored, faint) with the true mean signal `h` overlaid (black), and `plot_ece_terms`, which plots the raw pairwise ECE term over time (gray), a rolling-window mean (blue), and the global mean the test actually uses (dashed red). Since $r = 0$, any visible drift in the rolling mean away from the global mean is a symptom of the mean shift leaking into the covariance estimate, not genuine correlation.

## Scenario 1: Flat

```{R}
params <- scenario(1, n = 1000, r = 0)
```

No mean shift: `h` is identically zero. This is the stationary baseline against which the other scenarios are compared.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Signal

```{R scenario-1-h}
X <- generate_data(params)
h_df <- tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), h = params$h[, 1])
X_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 1], series = "X1"),
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 2], series = "X2")
)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = X_df, aes(t, value, color = series), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = h_df, aes(t, h), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(X1 = "steelblue", X2 = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Scenario 1", x = "Index", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Trend

```{R scenario-1-trend}
plot_ece_terms(X)
```

:::

## Scenario 2: Square Wave

```{R}
params <- scenario(2, n = 1000, r = 0, L = 100)
```

The mean flips sign every `L` observations, producing a square wave with hard change points at `seq(L + 1, n, by = L)`. This is the canonical piecewise-constant mean-shift setting that segmentation-based methods are designed for.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Signal

```{R scenario-2-h}
X <- generate_data(params)
h_df <- tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), h = params$h[, 1])
X_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 1], series = "X1"),
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 2], series = "X2")
)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = X_df, aes(t, value, color = series), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = h_df, aes(t, h), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(X1 = "steelblue", X2 = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Scenario 2", x = "Index", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Trend

```{R scenario-2-trend}
plot_ece_terms(X)
```

:::

## Scenario 3: Sine Wave

```{R}
params <- scenario(3, n = 1000, r = 0, period = 365)
```

The mean drifts smoothly as $\sin(2\pi t / \text{period})$ — a slow seasonal trend with no discrete change points at all. ECE tolerates slow oscillation but degrades as the period shortens toward the sampling rate.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Signal

```{R scenario-3-h}
X <- generate_data(params)
h_df <- tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), h = params$h[, 1])
X_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 1], series = "X1"),
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 2], series = "X2")
)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = X_df, aes(t, value, color = series), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = h_df, aes(t, h), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(X1 = "steelblue", X2 = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Scenario 3", x = "Index", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Trend

```{R scenario-3-trend}
plot_ece_terms(X)
```

:::

## Scenario 4: Random Walk

```{R}
params <- scenario(4, n = 1000, r = 0)
```

The mean is a cumulative sum of iid Gaussian innovations, `cumsum(rnorm(n))`: a stochastic, unbounded drift with no fixed change points and no periodicity.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Signal

```{R scenario-4-h}
X <- generate_data(params)
h_df <- tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), h = params$h[, 1])
X_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 1], series = "X1"),
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 2], series = "X2")
)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = X_df, aes(t, value, color = series), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = h_df, aes(t, h), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(X1 = "steelblue", X2 = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Scenario 4", x = "Index", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Trend

```{R scenario-4-trend}
plot_ece_terms(X)
```

:::

## Scenario 5: Semi Random Walk

```{R}
params <- scenario(5, n = 1000, r = 0, L = 4, prob = 0.10)
```

The series is broken into blocks of length `L`; each block is a change point with probability `prob`, and at each change point the mean jumps by a Gaussian step. Between change points the mean is flat. This interpolates between Scenario 1 (no jumps) and Scenario 2 (jumps everywhere), and is the only scenario with both flat segments and irregular, randomly-spaced change points.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Signal

```{R scenario-5-h}
X <- generate_data(params)
h_df <- tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), h = params$h[, 1])
X_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 1], series = "X1"),
  tibble(t = seq_len(params$n), value = X[, 2], series = "X2")
)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = X_df, aes(t, value, color = series), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = h_df, aes(t, h), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(X1 = "steelblue", X2 = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Scenario 5", x = "Index", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Trend

```{R scenario-5-trend}
plot_ece_terms(X)
```

:::
